newsitem.title: USA: Senetek's INVICORP gets positive feedback.
newsitem.headline: Senetek's INVICORP gets positive feedback.

text.p: Senetek PLC said Wednesday that its INVICORP drug therapy for treating erectile dysfunction in males has received a positive evaluation from most of the patients who have completed diaries for Phase III clinical trials.
The trials are being conducted at 16 sites throughout the United Kingdom.
In addition, more than 200 patients currently are being prescribed INVICORP under their physician's responsibility, it added.
Senetek, which is based in London but has operations in St. Louis, said it expects to conclude these clinical trials in the near term.

It will submit product licensing applications early next year for approval to market the drug in a number of European countries. Pan-European approval then will be sought during the second half of 1997, it added.
INVICORP is an injectable formulation of vasoactive intestinal polypeptide in combination with phentolamine, an adrenergic drug.
INVICORP can be delivered using the MEIS Auto Injector, a self-injection process.

"So popular has INVICORP become during Phase III studies that many patients have requested that the therapy be made available to them after completing their clinical trial participation, with the result that several doctors are now prescribing INVICORP as first-line treatment for their more seriously impaired patients," Roger Oakes, chief executive officer of Senetek's pharmaceuticals business unit, said in a statement.
